messages.content:
<ticket id="t011">
Our team of 12 uses Lumen daily. We would pay extra for a way to see who edited a note and when, like a version history with names. Right now we cannot tell who deleted a paragraph.
</ticket>

<category>feature_request</category>
<findings>
none
</findings>

Your task: Check whether Lumen currently offers any note version history, edit attribution, or activity log showing who edited or deleted content and when. Report what exists, what plan or tier it applies to, and any known limits. Do not promise a roadmap date.

I have been using Lumen for about two years now, mostly for my research as a graduate student in marine biology, and I have accumulated several hundred notes spread across roughly thirty notebooks. Recently my advisor suggested that I reorganize everything by project rather than by date, and I would like to do this without losing the links between notes, because I use a lot of internal links to connect field observations with literature summaries. My question is: if I move a note from one notebook to another, do the links that point to that note keep working? And if I merge two notebooks, what happens to the comments and the edit history? I could not find a clear answer in the help center, and I do not want to try it on my real data first. content.text: I found no record that Lumen offers named edit attribution or a who-deleted-what activity log. Ticket t020 mentions a "version history" in the app, but the customer does not say whether it records editor names, and it showed nothing for a note that was lost, so I could not confirm what it covers. My search tools do not include plan or tier information or help-center articles, so I cannot say which plan would include any such feature or what its limits are. Related tickets t022 (whether edit history survives notebook merges) and t055 (audit-trail export for legal) have no answer recorded.
